diagnosis_explanation: Your gallbladder has small stones in it. These stones can cause pain. This is called symptomatic cholelithiasis.
medication_rationale:
Ciprofloxacin:
This medicine fights certain types of bacteria. It was given to help with your infection. You might feel an upset stomach. This is common. Call your doctor if you get a rash or have trouble breathing.

Omeprazole:
This medicine lowers the amount of acid in your stomach. It can help with pain or healing in your stomach. You might get a headache. This is not usually a problem. Call your doctor if you get severe stomach pain or black, tarry stools.

Colace:
This medicine softens your stools. It makes it easier to have a bowel movement. You may notice your bowel movements become more regular. This is normal. Call your doctor if you have stomach cramps or bloating that does not go away.

Percocet:
This medicine helps relieve moderate to severe pain. You may feel sleepy or dizzy. This is common. Do not drive or use machines if you feel this way. Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing or are very constipated.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You may feel tired and sore after your procedure.
- You can shower, but keep your wound clean and dry.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 10 pounds.
- You cannot drive for 1 to 2 weeks.
- Eat only clear liquids for the first 48 hours.
- You can return to your Medifast diet after 48 hours.
- Call your doctor if you have shortness of breath or chest pain.
- Your goal this week is to walk around your home each day.

**Week 2:**
- You should start to feel a little more energy this week.
- Keep your wound clean and dry.
- You can resume driving if you can stop in an emergency.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 10 pounds.
- Avoid any strenuous activity.
- Your goal this week is to walk a bit longer each day.
- Call your doctor if your temperature is over 101.5 degrees.
- Call your doctor if you have severe nausea or vomiting.

**Week 3:**
- You may feel much less pain this week.
- You can do light activities but no heavy lifting.
- You can drive if you can stop in an emergency.
- Continue to keep your wound clean and dry.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 10 to 15 minutes daily.
- Call your doctor if you have new or worsening abdominal pain.
- Call your doctor if your wound looks red, swollen, or smells bad.

**Week 4:**
- You should have more energy and feel more comfortable.
- You can increase your daily walking.
- You can drive if you can stop in an emergency.
- Avoid heavy lifting and strenuous activity.
- Your goal this week is to walk outside for 20 minutes daily.
- Call your doctor if you have any breathing troubles.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Most people feel better after 4 weeks.
- Keep your wound clean and dry.
- Continue to avoid heavy lifting and strenuous activity.
- Listen to your body and rest when you need to.
- You should see steady progress each week.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Shortness of breath: Your body needs oxygen now.
- Chest pain: Your heart needs help now.
- Abdominal pain: This could be a sign of trouble.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Temperature over 101.5: You may have an infection.
- Intractable nausea: You cannot keep fluids down.
- Vomiting: You cannot keep fluids down.
- Wound redness or swelling: This means infection is spreading.
- Foul wound drainage: This means infection is spreading.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
